summary: Full-extraction pass over 16 stored Montenegrin documents: EC country reports 2019-2024, Government reports on the special investment programme for 2021 (scanned, read by OCR) and the 2026 status reports, and four Official Gazette decisions (OCR). Government Decision of 22 Nov 2018 (Službeni list CG 79/2018, 5 image-only pages) creating the special investment programme: competent authority; intermediary and due-diligence agents chosen by public call, licence conditions (3 years' experience, 3 states incl. one EU; criminal record), one-year licences renewable twice, licence fee EUR 50,000 a year for intermediaries (free for due-diligence agents), agent lists; applicant criteria (fees EUR 15,000 / 10,000 per family member up to four / 50,000 each further; EUR 100,000 escrow for less developed municipalities; EUR 450,000 or 250,000 escrow for a listed development project; criminal record; positive due diligence incl. source of funds); tourism project criteria (stars, EUR 15m/5m minimum investment, 80/25 employees, 60/35 units); agriculture/industry projects; application and family members; procedure (report to the PM, Interior Ministry, escrow transfer checked by an independent auditor); cap of 2,000 applications; loss of citizenship for false data without refund; in force on the eighth day after publication, applies 1 Jan 2019-31 Dec 2021. Fees, donation, project investment amounts and two events were already in the dataset; this pass adds the remaining numeric rules as terms (agent licence fee, cap, tourism project thresholds, adult-child age). Not recorded as terms because the document writes them in words: licence validity of one year renewable twice, agents' three years' experience in three states, the disqualifying prison sentence of more than one year. The entry-into-force date (eighth day after publication) is not recorded as an event because the document does not print the date.

Government Decision of 30 Dec 2021 amending the programme decision (Službeni list CG 143/2021, 2 image-only pages): innovation added to the purpose; agent licences renewable three times instead of twice; new EUR 100,000 escrow payment for the Innovation Fund; listed tourism projects need a first-demand bank guarantee of 50% of the minimum investment, to be delivered within 30 days or the project is struck off; new list of documents; escrow transfer covers the new payment; programme extended to 31 Dec 2022; in force on publication. Innovation Fund term and the extension event were already in the dataset; this pass adds the guarantee terms and the licence-renewal event.

Government Decision of 23 Jun 2022 amending the programme decision (Službeni list CG 68/2022, 1 image-only page): project bank guarantee changed from 50% of the minimum investment to EUR 1,000,000; ministry name changed; children born after the application during the programme count as family members, with an application fee of EUR 50,000 per such child; investors may replace their guarantee within 45 days to get the old one returned; in force on publication. The child fee and the guarantee event were already in the dataset; this pass adds the guarantee amount and the 45-day window as terms.

Government Decision of 30 Jun 2023 (Službeni list CG 67/2023, 1 image-only page) adding art. 5e to the general decision on criteria for citizenship in the interest of Montenegro: licences of intermediary and due-diligence agents stay valid until decisions on all programme applications filed by 31 Dec 2022; in force on publication. No figures besides dates and gazette numbers; the rule is already recorded as an event.

European Commission Montenegro 2019 Report (SWD(2019) 217, 110 pp.), covering all accession chapters. Programme content: Chapter 23 (PDF pp. 32-33) notes the November 2018 decision introducing the scheme and its launch in January 2019 and asks for robust monitoring; Chapter 4 (PDF p. 59-60) gives a minimum investment of EUR 365,000 and asks for AML risk assessment and enhanced due diligence. The rest (economy, other chapters, readmission, statistics on acquisition of citizenship generally) is out of scope. The launch is already in the events table from the Decision.

European Commission Montenegro 2020 Report (SWD(2020) 353, 131 pp.). Programme content: Chapter 23 (PDF p. 43) and Chapter 4 (PDF pp. 75-77): 24 applications received, 5 rejected after due diligence, 5 with final decisions, one passport issued in 2020 to a Russian citizen (already in the dataset), others delayed by COVID-19; minimum investment EUR 350,000; December 2019 amendments to the citizenship law covering family members (event already in the dataset from intl-ec-swd-2020-132); AML recommendations. The rest of the report is out of scope.

European Commission Montenegro 2021 Report (SWD(2021) 293, 123 pp.). Programme content: Chapter 23 (PDF p. 40): March 2021 decision not to prolong the scheme beyond 2021 (event already in the dataset from intl-ec-com-2021-602), licences issued to three intermediary and two due-diligence agents (written as words), 81 applicants and 185 family members with positive decisions by mid-2021 (already in the dataset); the same 81/185 repeated 'so far' in Chapter 4 (PDF p. 77) and not recorded twice; phase-out recommendations (PDF pp. 8, 51, 58, 72, 75-76). The rest is out of scope.

European Commission Montenegro 2022 Report (SWD(2022) 335, 135 pp.). Programme content: Chapter 23 (PDF pp. 46, 61) and Chapter 4 (PDF pp. 84-85): December 2021 extension to December 2022, March 2022 stricter checks freezing pending applications, May 2022 extra checks on Russian and Belarusian applicants and revocation procedure (no case found), June 2022 lowering of the bank guarantee from EUR 2.5 million to EUR 1 million and children born after the application; statistics January 2019-May 2022: 934 applications counted per person (279 applicants, 655 family members), 409 accepted, 3 rejected, 522 under evaluation (152 applicants, 370 family members), 333 passports (69 in the first four months of 2022), over 70% to Russian citizens; recommendations to terminate (pp. 9, 80). Chapter 4 repeats the statistics. Previously recorded: received 279/655, approved 409, rejected 3, pending 152 and 522, passports 333 and 69, March 2022 event. The rest is out of scope.

European Commission Montenegro 2023 Report (SWD(2023) 694, 143 pp.). Programme content: scheme phased out/expired at end 2022 (pp. 9, 52, 67, 70, 93-94); 556 applications January 2019-December 2022 (556 applicants, 1,281 family members); 954 positive decisions by 15 Jun 2023 (293 applicants, 661 family members); 398 pending on 15 Jun 2023 (with 710 family members, p. 94); source-of-funds screening by external providers; May 2023 Coordinating Body; Russia and UAE FDI shares linked to the programme (p. 78, no programme figure); Innovation Fund financed from programme receipts without due diligence (p. 110, no figure). Previously recorded: 556/1,281 received, 293 and 661 approved, 954 naturalised, 398 pending, two events. Not recorded: other numbers on those pages concern FDI shares and industrial-policy spending, not the programme. The rest is out of scope.
